title: Benford's Law: Why Do So Many Numbers Start With 1?
question: Why do the leading digits of real-world data follow a predictable, lopsided distribution instead of being uniform?
summary: About 30% of numbers in natural datasets begin with 1 and fewer than 5% with 9. Logarithms, scale invariance, and mixtures of distributions explain this surprising pattern, now a tool for detecting fraud.
